corpusSummary: Across more than 40 2026 records spanning human–AI interaction, health, climate, education, and AI-enabled research, this corpus shows large language models being used as both analytical tools and decision-making agents. It reveals methodological opportunities and governance needs, with mixed findings on personalization and trust, and persistent concerns about misinformation, bias, safety, ethics, and energy costs.

themes.name: LLMs for social science methods and governance
themes.description: Methodological and governance-oriented use of LLMs in social science, evidenced by papers on public policy analysis, urban participatory planning, AI-assisted coding and content analysis, and AI-enabled research workflows.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and adoption
themes.description: Across domains from education and work to health and everyday life, studies show that trust, perceived credibility, presentation style, social networks, and embodied interfaces shape AI adoption and interaction outcomes.

themes.name: AI in health, wellbeing, and health communication
themes.description: Health and wellbeing literature analyzes AI-generated misinformation, AI-assisted counseling, patient education quality, and health communication, revealing both benefits and safety and ethics concerns.

themes.name: AI in education, learning, and literacy
themes.description: Education-focused work reports mixed effects of GenAI on learning, pedagogy, assessment, AI literacy, and teacher adoption, with potential for personalization alongside risks of overreliance and skill erosion.
